segments.text: ​​​ ​Shiori~n!​ ​​
​​​ ​Welcome aboard, dear traveler, to:​ ​​
​​​ ​the Odyssey of the Seas.​ ​​
​​​ ​Seven days.​ ​​
​​​ ​One ship.​ ​​

​​​ ​And a whole lineup of performances​ ​​
​​ ​and sights to "sea."​ ​​
​​​ ​As your special little preview:​ ​​
​​​ ​high flying acrobatics,​ ​​
​​​ ​aerial stunts,​ ​​
​​​ ​futuristic drone shows,​ ​​
​​​ ​laser-lit dance stages,​ ​​
​​​ ​and even a little bit of magic​ ​​

​​​ ​before wrapping it all up with a visit to​ ​​
​​ ​one of NASA's legendary launch sites.​ ​​
​​​ ​So sit back, relax,​ ​​

​​​ ​and join me in reliving some​ ​​
​​ ​of my favorite memories.​ ​​
​​​ ​After security clearance, there's a bit of a wait​ ​​
​​​ ​while rooms get prepped for travelers.​ ​​
​​​ ​Most people head straight for the buffets or the pool,​ ​​
​​​ ​but I got distracted by this cute holiday display!​ ​​
​​​ ​You cannot eat these.​ ​​
​​​ ​Or so it claims.​ ​​
​​​ ​It's just for show.​ ​​

​​​ ​Meant to be admired while​ ​​
​​ ​I try to dodge people in frame​ ​​
​​​ ​so I don't have to blur fifty faces.​ ​​
​​​ ​It wasn't just gingerbread either.​ ​​
​​​ ​There were all sorts of cookie-looking houses,​ ​​
​​​ ​festive toy kits mashes together...​ ​​

​​​ ​Plus little diorama trees and​ ​​
​​ ​train sets scattered all over.​ ​​
​​​ ​Room tour!​ ​​
​​​ ​The cabins are a decent size.​ ​​
​​​ ​Mine didn't come with a window, though,​ ​​

​​​ ​so I completely lost track of time​ ​​
​​ ​and slept in most days.​ ​​
​​​ ​There's plenty of closet and wardrobe space,​ ​​
​​​ ​fancy wooden hangers included.​ ​​

​​​ ​And possibly an unwanted guest​ ​​
​​ ​if you're not careful.​ ​​
​​​ ​The bed was super comfy.​ ​​
​​​ ​The pillows were nice and chubby,​ ​​
​​​ ​and the blanket was extra fluffy.​ ​​
​​​ ​Way nicer than my bed at home, to be honest.​ ​​
​​​ ​Behind the wardrobe doors, you'll find a fridge,​ ​​
​​​ ​hairdryer,​ ​​
​​​ ​daily itinerary,​ ​​

​​​ ​and just shelf space if you're​ ​​
​​ ​the type to actually unpack.​ ​​

​​​ ​I just open my suitcase like it's a​ ​​
​​ ​treasure chest and hunt for loot.​ ​​
​​​ ​The bathroom!​ ​​
​​​ ​Spacious shower...​ ​​
​​​ ​Sanitary disposal bags...​ ​​
​​​ ​Traveler-sized soap, shampoo, conditioner...​ ​​
​​​ ​Fancy shmancy glass cups and extra amenities.​ ​​
​​​ ​Overall, the bathroom was roomier than I expected.​ ​​
​​​ ​So yeah, that's my home base!​ ​​
​​​ ​For seven days.​ ​​

​​​ ​After unpacking, there's not a whole​ ​​
​​ ​lot to do while you're out at sea,​ ​​
​​​ ​unless you're into ship activities.​ ​​
​​​ ​They've got things like rock climbing,​ ​​
​​​ ​dance classes,​ ​​

​​​ ​game nights, spa treatments,​ ​​
​​ ​and fitness appointments.​ ​​
​​​ ​Oh, and they offer wellness consultations.​ ​​

​​​ ​You can book skin assessments and body​ ​​
​​ ​composition scans with actual specialists.​ ​​

​​​ ​I ended up booking a massage through it,​ ​​
​​ ​which I'll talk about later.​ ​​

​​​ ​For the first two days, I mostly just wandered​ ​​
​​ ​around to see what the ship had going on.​ ​​
​​​ ​Oooh! Chair!​ ​​
​​​ ​There's a central hub area,​ ​​

​​​ ​but it's smaller than the one​ ​​
​​ ​on the last ship I was on.​ ​​
​​​ ​The whole ship felt a bit older and smaller.​ ​​

​​​ ​There were a few shopping spots,​ ​​
​​ ​but nothing huge.​ ​​
​​​ ​two lounges,​ ​​
​​​ ​some merch stores,​ ​​

​​​ ​and a mix of luxury shops selling​ ​​
​​ ​perfumes, watches, and jewelry.​ ​​

​​​ ​There were also smaller stalls​ ​​
​​ ​with more affordable jewelry​ ​​
​​​ ​and the usual souvenir stuff.​ ​​
​​​ ​And you know... There's like...​ ​​
​​​ ​Gambling. Casinos.​ ​​
​​​ ​For gacha addicts.​ ​​
​​​ ​But yeah!​ ​​
​​​ ​My favorite rooms for the entire ship...​ ​​

​​​ ​I didn't spend a lot of time there,​ ​​
​​ ​but the prettiest sights were the pools.​ ​​
​​​ ​Especially at night.​ ​​

​​​ ​I did swim a bit, but most days were​ ​​
​​ ​too cold to be doing that.​ ​​
​​​ ​Once we crossed into warmer weather, it was fine.​ ​​
​​​ ​We went during winter.​ ​​
​​​ ​(Mostly because it's cheaper that time of year.)​ ​​

​​​ ​But honestly, most of my relatives were​ ​​
​​ ​into the gambling stuff anyway,​ ​​
​​​ ​so it really didn't matter.​ ​​
​​​ ​Kind of ironic.​ ​​
​​​ ​There's also the solarium, an adults-only area.​ ​​
​​​ ​Just a quiet spot for relaxing.​ ​​
​​​ ​No kids to cry and scream in your ears.​ ​​

​​​ ​I swam there once,​ ​​
​​ ​just under one of the water spouts.​ ​​

​​​ ​It's temperature-controlled,​ ​​
​​ ​so way warmer than the public pool space.​ ​​
​​​ ​Would absolutely recommend.​ ​​

​​​ ​It's near the same area where​ ​​
​​ ​you can get unlimited ice cream,​ ​​
​​​ ​so I abused that.​ ​​

​​​ ​Most of my time on the ship was spent​ ​​
​​ ​searching for little ducklings.​ ​​
​​​ ​There's a fun tradition on this cruise line​ ​​

​​​ ​where passengers hide rubber duck toys​ ​​
​​ ​in random nooks and crannies.​ ​​
​​​ ​If you find one? You get to keep it!​ ​​
​​​ ​Basically a ship-wide duck hunt.​ ​​

​​​ ​I spent each day combing​ ​​
​​ ​each floor to try my luck,​ ​​

​​​ ​and since I was competing​ ​​
​​ ​with so many passengers,​ ​​
​​​ ​it was pretty tough to find them.​ ​​
​​​ ​But I managed!​ ​​

​​​ ​Along the way, I got to see some​ ​​
​​ ​really creative door decor.​ ​​
​​​ ​There was a meme cat door,​ ​​
​​​ ​tropical and sea-themed setups...​ ​​
​​​ ​This funny one by some old people.​ ​​
​​​ ​I'm kidding, I'm kidding.​ ​​
​​​ ​My favorite door.​ ​​
​​​ ​Look, how nice of them.​ ​​
​​​ ​Look what we have...​ ​​

​​​ ​And of course, Christmas lights and​ ​​
​​ ​stockings for some holiday cheer.​ ​​
​​​ ​Another thing I checked out –​ ​​

​​​ ​and by that, I mean I recorded​ ​​
​​ ​a stranger getting their drink –​ ​​
​​​ ​was this robotic drink mixer.​ ​​

​​​ ​There are two blue mechanical​ ​​
​​ ​arms attached to a table​ ​​
​​​ ​that reach up to the ceiling, grab bottles,​ ​​
​​​ ​and start shaking them like a bartender.​ ​​

​​​ ​And then nearby, there's just a human cleaner​ ​​
​​ ​in case they spill the drink.​ ​​
​​​ ​Which I found kind of funny.​ ​​

​​​ ​And when I returned to my room,​ ​​
​​ ​I'm greeted by...​ ​​
​​​ ​I actually have no idea what this is.​ ​​
​​​ ​I think it's an elephant?​ ​​
​​​ ​But it's pretty cute!​ ​​
​​​ ​Finally land!​ ​​
​​​ ​At least a wee bit of it.​ ​​
​​​ ​After two full days at sea,​ ​​

​​​ ​we finally docked at a small island​ ​​
​​ ​known as CocoCay.​ ​​
​​​ ​It's packed with mini water parks,​ ​​
​​​ ​tropical buffets,​ ​​
​​​ ​swim-up bars,​ ​​

​​​ ​And exclusive gated areas​ ​​
​​ ​for those wanting a quieter time​ ​​
​​​ ​and willing to fork over some extra cash.​ ​​

​​​ ​I went for the buffet first​ ​​
​​ ​since was complimentary.​ ​​

​​​ ​The food was pretty basic:​ ​​
​​ ​hot dogs and hamburgers.​ ​​

​​​ ​It's convenient beach-ready food​ ​​
​​ ​since the island is so isolated.​ ​​
​​​ ​Every ingredient has to be ferried in by boat.​ ​​

​​​ ​After eating, I wandered off to find​ ​​
​​ ​the quietest ​free beach section I could find.​ ​​

​​​ ​The weather was perfect –​ ​​
​​ ​vibrant blue skies and seas.​ ​​
​​​ ​The water... was freezing.​ ​​
​​​ ​But I swam anyway!​ ​​
​​​ ​I was already wearing a bathing suit,​ ​​

​​​ ​and I didn't come wandering this far​ ​​
​​ ​just to do nothing.​ ​​

​​​ ​So I braved it all,​ ​​
​​ ​and shivered my Shioreos off.​ ​​

​​​ ​After a fun day in the sun,​ ​​
​​ ​I went back to the ship​ ​​
​​​ ​and got to watch a live performance.​ ​​
​​​ ​The next two days were spent stuck out at sea.​ ​​
​​​ ​Due to rough weather, the ship couldn't dock,​ ​​
​​​ ​so we skipped an entire port day.​ ​​

​​​ ​Things got bad enough that vomit bags​ ​​
​​ ​were distributed near the stairs at each floor.​ ​​
​​​ ​Even I had to take sea sickness medicine,​ ​​
​​​ ​and I didn't even know I could get sea sick.​ ​​
​​​ ​Once the ocean finally calmed down,​ ​​
​​​ ​I booked myself a massage to relax.​ ​​

​​​ ​This was my first ever massage,​ ​​
​​ ​and I wasn't sure what to expect.​ ​​
​​​ ​So you lie face down on a padded table.​ ​​
​​​ ​There's a towel draped over your back,​ ​​

​​​ ​and they play this low ambient​ ​​
​​ ​music around the room.​ ​​

​​​ ​The lights were dim and they give you an option​ ​​
​​ ​of what type of scent you want in the air.​ ​​
​​​ ​And I chose a full body massage,​ ​​

​​​ ​which covers everything from my lower legs​ ​​
​​ ​and thighs, to my back and shoulders.​ ​​
​​​ ​You get about an hour in the room,​ ​​

​​​ ​and after the massage,​ ​​
​​ ​they give you recommendations​ ​​
​​​ ​on which part of the body you should work on.​ ​​

​​​ ​For example, they told me that I could get​ ​​
​​ ​this type of oil for this area,​ ​​
​​​ ​and you should try to massage it more.​ ​​
​​​ ​And I'm like, yeah...​ ​​
​​​ ​I'm never gonna see this again.​ ​​

​​​ ​After the massage, aboard the ship​ ​​
​​ ​are several specialty restaurants,​ ​​

​​​ ​and Izumi was a hibachi spot we'd pass by​ ​​
​​ ​constantly on the way to the pool deck.​ ​​
​​​ ​For those who don't know,​ ​​
​​​ ​hibachi restaurants are dine-in areas​ ​​
​​​ ​where the chef cooks right in front of you.​ ​​
​​​ ​It's an interactive experience.​ ​​

​​​ ​Maybe a little chaotic since they might​ ​​
​​ ​toss a shrimp or egg your way.​ ​​

​​​ ​And if your reflexes aren't that great,​ ​​
​​ ​it might be a bit daunting.​ ​​
​​​ ​The chef was pretty fun.​ ​​

​​​ ​He'd flip an egg into the air​ ​​
​​ ​with a spatula without cracking it,​ ​​
​​​ ​roll it across his hat,​ ​​
​​​ ​and then he would juggle the spatulas.​ ​​
​​​ ​The food was solid. Nice and savory.​ ​​

​​​ ​I'd say overall, it's...​ ​​
​​ ​an entertaining experience,​ ​​

​​​ ​but if you're someone who prefers quieter meals,​ ​​
​​ ​this would not be the place for you.​ ​​

​​​ ​But if you have children or​ ​​
​​ ​enjoy a bit of excitement,​ ​​
​​​ ​it might be worth to give it a try.​ ​​
​​​ ​Just not aboard a cruise ship.​ ​​
​​​ ​A specialty restaurant like this was not cheap here.​ ​​

​​​ ​For a family this size, you're probably looking​ ​​
​​ ​at 600 bucks for the full meal and show.​ ​​
​​​ ​So yeah, just to let you know.​ ​​
​​​ ​Ever heard of NASA?​ ​​
​​​ ​It's America's main research agency​ ​​

​​​ ​dedicated to exploring space and​ ​​
​​ ​everything beyond the stars.​ ​​
​​​ ​In the gator-infested wetlands of Florida,​ ​​

​​​ ​NASA operates one of its major field centers:​ ​​
​​ ​the Kennedy Space Center,​ ​​
​​​ ​which serves as their primary launch site.​ ​​

​​​ ​When you first walk in,​ ​​
​​ ​you'll see space-themed trash cans​ ​​

​​​ ​and ticket booths,​ ​​
​​ ​which I found kind of cute.​ ​​
​​​ ​Inside, you'll find historical exhibits,​ ​​
​​​ ​short documentary clips,​ ​​

​​​ ​and replicas or real artifacts​ ​​
​​ ​from past space missions.​ ​​

​​​ ​In the Apollo/Saturn V Center,​ ​​
​​ ​you can get a front row seat​ ​​
​​​ ​into a recreated launch control room.​ ​​

​​​ ​From here, you can experience what it was like​ ​​
​​ ​for operators to prepare for takeoff.​ ​​

​​​ ​It comes complete with (I think)​ ​​
​​ ​original equipment,​ ​​
​​​ ​countdown clocks,​ ​​

​​​ ​and a dramatic presentation​ ​​
​​ ​that simulates a launch.​ ​​
​​​ ​Once you've finished the presentation,​ ​​
​​​ ​you'll be able to freely wander into the next room​ ​​
​​​ ​where this massive rocket is located.​ ​​

​​​ ​This right here holds the title of​ ​​
​​ ​the largest rocket ever flown​ ​​

​​​ ​and stands at a whopping 363 feet,​ ​​
​​ ​or 111 meters tall.​ ​​

​​​ ​Nearby, you'll find displays like Apollo 14's​ ​​
​​ ​command module, nicknamed Kitty Hawk.​ ​​
​​​ ​Oddly cute for what it is.​ ​​

​​​ ​For those who don't know,​ ​​
​​ ​the Apollo spacecraft has two components:​ ​​
​​​ ​the Service Module and Command Module.​ ​​

​​​ ​The Service one handles life support, power,​ ​​
​​ ​and propulsion while in space,​ ​​
​​​ ​while the Command one houses the living quarters​ ​​

​​​ ​complete with mission computers​ ​​
​​ ​and navigation systems.​ ​​

​​​ ​The Service Module is the part that​ ​​
​​ ​detaches when it returns to Earth,​ ​​

​​​ ​so Kitty Hawk here is the only part of​ ​​
​​ ​the spacecraft to return from the mission.​ ​​

​​​ ​But yeah, there's just so much​ ​​
​​ ​tech on display here.​ ​​
​​​ ​Just look at the complexity of this rocket engine.​ ​​

​​​ ​Layers of wiring and piping​ ​​
​​ ​that makes my brain hurt.​ ​​
​​​ ​Then there's the retired Space Shuttle Atlantis,​ ​​
​​​ ​which flew 33 missions over 26 years.​ ​​

​​​ ​To top it off, you can experience a simulated​ ​​
​​ ​launch in the Shuttle flight simulator.​ ​​
​​​ ​After a safety briefing and info about G-force,​ ​​
​​​ ​you're strapped into a launch seat.​ ​​

​​​ ​The room begins to rumble intensely​ ​​
​​ ​as the shuttle tilts back,​ ​​
​​​ ​and then you "launch" into space,​ ​​
​​​ ​ending with a view of Earth from orbit.​ ​​
​​​ ​Wave goodbye to the external tank,​ ​​
​​​ ​and say hello to outer space.​ ​​

​​​ ​And that was the peak experience​ ​​
​​ ​of my cruise ship vacation.​ ​​

​​​ ​Naturally, the last day is just me​ ​​
​​ ​heading back home, so...​ ​​
​​​ ​From chasing ducklings around the deck,​ ​​

​​​ ​catching nightly shows with acrobatics,​ ​​
​​ ​singers, and dancers,​ ​​
​​​ ​taking a freezing swim,​ ​​

​​​ ​to ending it all with a full tour​ ​​
​​ ​through space history...​ ​​
​​​ ​Yeah. One heck of a trip.​ ​​
​​​ ​And if you enjoyed the video,​ ​​
​​​ ​go ahead and touch some grass too when you can.​ ​​
​​​ ​Until then. Shiori~n!​ ​​
